old: Letting a younger feeling-state speak doesn’t mean handing adult judgment to an outside caretaker or trying to become literally younger. Wonder, play, vivid sensation, vulnerability, honest need, or the wish to carry fewer decisions can all come forward while the internal adult remains present.
new: You can choose to let the parts of you that feel younger express themselves without handing over the adult part of you to the caretaker in the other person or without actually going back in age. In this way, you can access all of the positive aspects of what it can be like to feel younger such as feeling wonder, silliness, approaching things through the senses more, feeling it’s ok to be vulnerable, to let someone take care of you, to feel need, and to want to offload some decision making.

old: When love is available, the younger state doesn’t have to believe in it before you can offer it. Trust can question your promises, remember failures of protection, and take its time. Love can remain present while that happens.
“Okay. I believe that you don’t believe me. I still love you. You don’t have to love me back. Tell me what feels unsafe.”

That isn’t a way to end the complaint. Listen for what is true in it and answer seriously. Hearing anger without retaliation, admitting a real failure, and repairing after an internal attack are evidence alongside meals, boundaries, appointments, and kept promises. Non-retaliation expresses love; it shouldn’t replace love with a colder performance of good behavior.

Notice what each position teaches the others. A vow followed by blame when it is doubted teaches that love depends on receiving it correctly. The blaming voice and the voice making the vow may be different positions, the same position, or a blend. Don’t decide from the person’s chronological age.

When a younger version of you becomes the defendant, ask what they understood then, what options they could see and tolerate, and what happened because of the choice. Harm can require responsibility and repair. Punishment cannot retroactively create the capacity that was missing.
new: What if the "child" doesn't believe you love him/her? It is possible to love him/her even if he/she doesn't believe you love him/her. It is possible for trust to take it's time.
You could say something like, "Okay. I believe that you don't believe me. But I still love you. And you don't have to love me. Please tell me what is not okay."

Then respond to the complaints that are sure to come. Because even if he/she is coming from a place that is not completely "right," there will likely be something true in what he/she is saying. Do what you can to show your love for him/her. This might include some or all of the following: Learning to listen to him/her when he/she is angry without hitting back. Owning what was not okay. Working on changing yourself so that you are less likely to turn on him/her. Finding other ways to make up to him/her for what you did. Finding other ways to show your love for him/her (this might include taking care of him/her, such as by buying and cooking food for him/her, setting limits for him/her, taking him/her to the doctor when he/she needs it, and doing what you said you would do). Just not hitting back is not enough. You need to love your "inner child."

Be aware of what you are teaching your other positions. For example, are you teaching your "inner child" that you are going to love him/her no matter what? Or are you teaching him/her that it is his/her responsibility to believe your love for him/her, and that if he/she doesn't, it is his/her fault? Is it two separate positions, one making the vow to love the "inner child" no matter what, and the other blaming the "inner child" for not taking in your love? Or is it one position doing both of these things? Or are you blending them? It might not be chronological age.

When you're placing your younger self on trial, how valuable is it to consider how valuable it might have been for them to do what they did at the time, given what they knew at the time? How valuable is it to consider what options they had at the time and how tolerable they were? How valuable is it to consider what the consequences of their actions were at the time? How valuable is it to consider that, even though their actions at the time might have been harmful to you and others, punishing yourself now is not going to give them the capacity they needed at the time and that it's more useful to work on what you can do now to deal with the harm that was caused?
WORKING WITH YOUR INNER CHILD:

old: The Nurturer brings warmth without trying to rush the feeling away, and takes pleasure in the child’s company: “I’m glad you’re here.” The child needs to be enjoyed, not only comforted when hurt.
“It’s okay to feel this.” “I’m here.” “You don’t have to do anything right now.” “You are not too much.” “You can be small here.” “You can be angry here.” “You can be sad here.” “I will stay.”
new: The Nurturer: Some of the work you can do as the Nurturer is to enjoy your inner child. You don't have to move their feelings, just sit back and enjoy them. Be happy that they are there. Children need to be enjoyed! Say things to your inner child like:
It's okay to feel the way you're feeling.
I want you to know that I'm here for you.
You don't need to do anything right now.
It's okay. You're not too much. You can be small here.
You can be angry here.
You can be sad here.

old: The Protector turns warmth into something the child can believe.

“I will set the boundary.” “I will leave the unsafe conversation.” “I will stop texting the person who destabilizes us.” “I will eat.” “I will sleep.” “I will keep a small promise.” “I will not leave the child alone with adult consequences.”

This is where inner-child practice often turns decorative. The voice says loving things while the adult sends the destabilizing message, skips the meal, avoids the task, and breaks the promise. Trust begins when you handle the consequence.

If warmth is unavailable, a protective act can begin the relationship. Make it small enough to carry out and review what actually happened. A missed action might reflect fear, exhaustion, missing skills, a practical barrier, or a poor plan. Completion without immediate relief isn’t automatically failure, and a tick on a list doesn’t prove the action helped.
new: As the Protector, work with setting boundaries together. They can be simple like, "I'm going to leave this conversation because it's not safe" or "I'm going to stop texting the person who destabilizes me." It can be self-care boundaries like, "I'm going to eat" or "I'm going to get some sleep." It can be trust-related boundaries like, "I'm going to keep the promise to myself" or "I'm not going to leave you to do adult things by yourself."

A lot of times, inner child work doesn't work because people are doing all the fluffy stuff but then they go and text the person who is destabilizing them, or they don't eat, or they don't do whatever it is they're supposed to be doing. You build trust by being able to do adult things.

If it's hard to bring up the warm stuff, you can always do something to protect your inner child. Make sure they're small enough that you can actually do them. If you're not able to, figure out what's getting in the way of you doing them. Are you scared? Tired? Do you not know how to? Is there a practical thing that's getting in your way? Have you set yourself up to do it in a way that's likely to be successful? Don't make it so that doing it successfully is having to feel good about it, or being able to check it off a list.

old: Anxiety is often a Protector trying to prevent danger, shame, abandonment, failure, exposure, illness, rejection, loss of control, or a feeling it believes would be unbearable. Don’t begin by cross-examining it. Help the body first.
Body first. Inner child second. Inquiry third. Action fourth.
new: Remember that often the anxiety comes from a protector part of you, who is trying to help you, but who believes you are in danger, or may be shamed, or abandoned, or fail, or be exposed, or be sick, or be rejected, or lose control, or whatever. Therefore, instead of the interrogation above, start with yourself:
Always work with yourself in a series – first your body, then your inner child, then some inner work, then some action:

old: Start with the hand-on-heart, hand-on-solar-plexus practice.
“Little one, you are not alone. You do not have to solve this. I am here now. The adult is listening.”
Don’t recite the words like an incantation you’re hoping the subconscious will grade. Say them the way you’d speak to a frightened child you actually love.
new: Here is some inner child love. Put your hand over your heart and your other hand on your solar plexis, and say to yourself in a loving way, “Little one, you are not alone. You don’t have to fix this. I’m here now. The adult is listening.” Make sure you are actually talking to your inner child, who is scared to death.

old: Use this gently. Buteyko-style reduced breathing can help some people who overbreathe or panic, but don’t force breath holds. Air hunger can briefly increase anxiety before it settles, so go slowly.
Breathe through the nose. Let the inhale be small. Let the exhale be quiet. Pause only if comfortable. Let the breath become less dramatic. Stop if dizzy, strained, panicky, or medically concerned.
new: Then work on your reduced breathing / Buteyko’ breathing. (NOTE: there are some good things to be said for slowing your breathing down, if you are breathing too much, or panicked. However, please don’t hold your breath until you are air hungry, which can make you more anxious in the short term. Go slow on this.) Inhale small amounts through your nose, exhale quietly, and pause if you can. Can you make your breathing very quiet? If you feel bad, dizzy, or panicky, or have medical issues, STOP!

old: First, body. Feet, chair, breath, room.
Little one, I am here. Protector, thank you for warning me. You do not have to scream for me to listen.
If there is real action needed, show me one step. If there is no action needed, help the body stand down gently.
I will not abandon the signal. I will not worship the signal. I will listen, test, and act.
new: Where are my body parts? What are my feet doing? How is my body positioned in the chair? How is my body breathing? How is my body situated in the room?
If you’re there little one, let me know I’m here. Thank you protector for letting me know you’re here, you didn’t have to scream I got your message.

If there is something we need to do let me know what the first thing is that we need to do at this moment, if there is nothing to do help my body stand down. I’m not going to abandon you but I’m not going to worship you, I will listen to what you have to say and reality test it and then take some action.
